Prevention: Use varieties with known resistance to the main virus diseases, such as
Only use seeds from healthy plants (those which lack obvious virus symptoms, particularly leaf mosaics and mottling).
BlCMV, and other viruses on cowpea are seedborne.
Thoroughly remove weeds which may harbour aphids or other insect vectors.
Avoid planting in the dry season when plants may be more stressed and aphid vectors, for example, are more likely to feed on plants.
Monitoring: Regularly visit the crop, taking action as soon as symptoms are detected.
A patchwork of irregular light-coloured areas scattered across the surface of the leaf.
Mosaic symptoms are easier to see with the leaf held against the light.
Leaves that are smaller than expected.
They may have a wrinkled appearance and loss of colour.
BlCMV are transmitted by aphids, as is cowpea mosaic virus (CPMV).
Other viruses are transmitted by beetles or by whitefly.
It can be difficult to differentiate mosaics and mottling caused by different viruses (or combinations of them):

The discoloured areas in a leaf mosaic disease have a clearly defined boundary corresponding to leaf veins and differ from mottling, caused by different viruses on cowpea, where similar areas are not defined by veins.
Laboratory testing is essential for precise identification.
Good general advice on control can be given, however, based on a reliable field diagnosis of general virus attack.
Direct Control: Uproot and burn or bury (more than 50 cm deep) infected plants away from the crop field.
Collect and burn or deep plough crop residues after harvest to destroy insect vectors.
Do not plant new crops next to those that have the disease.
Early in the aphid infestation and during the early stages of the aphid life cycle, apply a mixture consisting of leaf extracts from papaya, teabush, Siam weed ( C. odorata ) and neem.
Do not use insecticides to control the aphids.
The time is short between an aphid sucking up the virus when it feeds on a diseased plant and spreading the virus as it feeds again on a healthy one.
By the time the insecticide has killed the aphid it has spread the virus.
